name: Brampton
intro: Brampton has more home-style tiffin kitchens per street than almost anywhere outside India, from Punjabi dhaba-style plans to Gujarati thalis and Jain tiffins.
scene: Demand here is driven by students, shift workers at the logistics parks along Highway 407 and 410, and families where both parents commute. Most kitchens run a weekly rotating menu, deliver lunch before noon and dinner from 6 pm, and quote monthly prices. Competition is intense, which keeps prices honest and makes trial weeks easy to find.
price: Weekday lunch plans commonly start around CA$160 to CA$250 a month for one person, which works out to roughly CA$8 to CA$12 a tiffin. Lunch-and-dinner plans run close to double. Paid trial meals are usually CA$10 to CA$15.
tip: Ask whether the roti count is fixed or unlimited, and whether delivery to student basements and upper floors costs extra. Several Brampton kitchens charge separately for doorstep delivery above the ground floor.

regulator.name: Peel Public Health: food operators
regulator.note: Ontario requires every home-based food business to notify its local public health unit before opening. In Brampton that is Peel Public Health, and you also need to contact the City about home-business rules.

name: Mississauga
intro: Mississauga's tiffin kitchens serve two very different crowds: families in Malton and Meadowvale, and office workers around Square One and the airport corridor.
scene: Office delivery is a bigger share of the market here than in Brampton, so many kitchens offer individual sealed boxes rather than steel tins and will deliver to reception desks. Expect lighter, lower-oil menus marketed to professionals alongside traditional Punjabi and South Indian plans.
price: Expect roughly CA$170 to CA$260 a month for weekday lunches, with office-delivery plans at the upper end. Single meals for office drop-offs are typically CA$11 to CA$15.
tip: If you need office delivery, confirm the cut-off time for changes and whether the kitchen can deliver to a building with a security desk. Ask for disposable or returnable containers up front.

regulator.name: Peel Public Health: food operators
regulator.note: Mississauga is also in Peel Region, so home kitchens notify Peel Public Health before opening and check the City's home-occupation rules.

name: Toronto
intro: Toronto's tiffin market is spread thin across a big city: Scarborough and Etobicoke have dense home-kitchen networks, while downtown relies on marketplace drops and office delivery.
scene: Because delivery distances are long, many Toronto kitchens deliver on fixed routes on fixed days. Regional cooking is unusually varied here: Bengali, Hyderabadi, Kerala, Tamil and Sri Lankan plans are all available if you ask, as are Caribbean and Indo-Caribbean tiffins.
price: Weekday lunch plans usually land between CA$180 and CA$280 a month. Downtown delivery and regional specialities sit at the top of that range.
tip: Check the delivery day pattern before you commit. Some downtown routes run three days a week rather than five, which changes the value of a monthly plan.

regulator.name: Ontario public health unit locator
regulator.note: Home-based food businesses in Toronto must notify Toronto Public Health before they start, and comply with Ontario's Food Premises Regulation.

name: Montréal
intro: Montréal's tiffin scene is smaller and more word-of-mouth than Toronto's, centred on Parc-Extension and the student neighbourhoods around the universities.
scene: Students at McGill, Concordia and Université de Montréal are the core market, so weekly plans and flexible pauses around exam periods are common. Many kitchens take orders in English, French, Hindi, Punjabi and Urdu. Supply is thinner than demand in parts of the West Island, which makes it a good city for a new kitchen.
price: Student-focused weekday lunch plans often start around CA$150 to CA$230 a month; family dinner plans cost more. Ask whether prices include QST.
tip: Ask whether the kitchen pauses for exam weeks and holidays without penalty, and whether delivery reaches residences and campus buildings or only the street.

regulator.name: Québec MAPAQ
regulator.note: In Québec, preparing food for sale generally requires a permit from the ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation (MAPAQ). On the island of Montréal, food inspection is carried out by the City of Montréal.

name: Surrey
intro: Surrey is the tiffin capital of the Lower Mainland, with a deep bench of Punjabi home kitchens around Newton and Strawberry Hill.
scene: Many Surrey kitchens also deliver to Delta, Langley and Abbotsford, and some cover Vancouver on set days. Sabzi-dal-roti plans dominate, but high-protein and lower-carb tiffins have grown fast with gym-going customers.
price: Weekday lunch plans commonly run about CA$170 to CA$260 a month. Kitchens that deliver beyond Surrey often add a weekly delivery fee.
tip: Ask exactly which days the kitchen covers your area. Cross-city routes are usually fixed, and a missed route day means no delivery that day.

regulator.name: Fraser Health
regulator.note: In British Columbia, food premises need approval from the regional health authority before operating. Surrey is served by Fraser Health's environmental health team.

name: Calgary
intro: Calgary's tiffin kitchens cluster in the northeast and serve a fast-growing newcomer population, oil-and-gas shift workers and downtown offices.
scene: Long winters make hot-delivery reliability the main selling point here, and the best kitchens deliver in insulated carriers on tight windows. Expect Punjabi, Gujarati and Kerala-style menus, plus Pakistani and Afghan home cooking.
price: Weekday lunch plans typically sit around CA$170 to CA$250 a month; downtown delivery may add a fee.
tip: In winter, ask how the food is kept hot between kitchen and door and what happens on extreme-cold days. A good kitchen has a clear answer.

regulator.name: Alberta Health Services: environmental public health
regulator.note: Selling prepared meals in Alberta requires a food handling permit from Alberta Health Services' environmental public health program.

name: New York City
intro: New York's tiffin cooks mostly work out of rented commercial kitchens in Queens and deliver into Manhattan offices and outer-borough homes.
scene: Jackson Heights and Richmond Hill anchor the South Asian and Indo-Caribbean food scene, and many tiffin businesses grew out of their restaurants and caterers. Office lunch drops in Midtown and Downtown are a large share of orders, so weekday-only plans dominate.
price: Expect roughly US$12 to US$18 a tiffin, or about US$240 to US$360 a month for weekday lunches. Manhattan delivery is usually at the high end.
tip: Ask where the food is cooked. In New York City the answer should be a permitted commercial kitchen, and a reputable operator will tell you which one.

regulator.name: NYC Health: food operators
regulator.note: Selling prepared meals in New York City requires a food service establishment permit from the Health Department, which is why most tiffin cooks rent permitted shared kitchens rather than cook at home.

name: Edison and Jersey City
intro: Central and north Jersey have one of the largest Indian-American populations in the US, and Oak Tree Road and India Square are where most tiffin businesses start.
scene: IT and pharma commuters drive weekday demand, and Gujarati and South Indian vegetarian plans are especially strong. Many services deliver along fixed routes through Edison, Iselin, Piscataway, Parsippany and Jersey City.
hoods: Oak Tree Road, Edison and Iselin
price: Expect around US$10 to US$15 a tiffin, or roughly US$200 to US$300 a month for weekday lunches.
tip: Jain and no-onion-garlic plans are widely available here, but ask whether they are cooked in a separate pot. If it matters to you, it matters to ask.

regulator.name: New Jersey Department of Health
regulator.note: New Jersey's cottage food permit covers only low-risk foods such as baked goods. Cooked meals must come from a licensed retail food establishment inspected by the local health department.

name: San Francisco Bay Area
intro: Fremont, Sunnyvale and Santa Clara have a dense, tech-driven tiffin market, and California's home-kitchen permit has made it easier for home cooks to sell legally.
scene: Demand peaks with hybrid office days, so many plans let you pick delivery days week by week. Telugu, Tamil, Kannada and Gujarati home cooking are all well represented, as are high-protein plans built for gym routines.
price: Expect around US$12 to US$18 a tiffin; plans that let you pick days are slightly dearer than fixed five-day plans.
tip: If you are ordering from a home kitchen, ask for its county MEHKO permit number. California requires permitted home kitchens to show it in their advertising.

regulator.name: California Department of Public Health: MEHKO
regulator.note: California lets counties opt in to Microenterprise Home Kitchen Operations: up to 30 meals a day, 90 a week and about US$100,000 a year, with a county health permit. Santa Clara and Alameda counties have opted in.

name: London
intro: London's tiffin culture runs from the Southall and Wembley home kitchens to City office lunches delivered in branded steel tins.
scene: Lunch delivery into offices in the City, Canary Wharf and the West End is a sizeable market, while family dinner plans dominate in Harrow, Hounslow and East Ham. Gujarati, Punjabi, Tamil and Sri Lankan cooking all have dedicated kitchens.
price: Expect roughly £7 to £11 a tiffin, or about £140 to £220 a month for weekday lunches. Central London office delivery costs more.
tip: Check the business's food hygiene rating on the Food Standards Agency website before you subscribe. Registered kitchens get inspected and rated.

regulator.name: GOV.UK: register a food business
regulator.note: In England, register with your local council at least 28 days before you start trading. Registration is free and covers food businesses run from home.

name: Leicester
intro: Leicester's Golden Mile on Belgrave Road has fed Gujarati families for decades, and its home-kitchen tiffin trade is one of the most established in Britain.
scene: Vegetarian and Jain plans are the norm rather than a niche here, and many kitchens also cater for weddings and religious events. University students are a growing second market.
price: Expect roughly £5 to £8 a tiffin, or about £110 to £170 a month for weekday lunches.
tip: Many Leicester kitchens are family operations that take orders by phone or WhatsApp only. Ask for a written weekly menu so you know what you are paying for.

regulator.name: GOV.UK: register a food business
regulator.note: Register with Leicester City Council at least 28 days before trading. Expect an inspection and a published food hygiene rating.

name: Melbourne
intro: Melbourne's tiffin services grew with its Indian and Sri Lankan communities in the west and south-east, and with a large international student population.
scene: Students and trade workers drive weekday demand, and many kitchens deliver along set routes through Tarneit, Truganina and Point Cook in the west and Dandenong and Clayton in the south-east.
price: Expect around A$12 to A$18 a tiffin, or roughly A$240 to A$360 a month for weekday lunches.
tip: Ask which suburbs fall inside the free delivery zone. Melbourne is spread out, and fees for suburbs outside the route can add up.

regulator.name: Victorian Department of Health
regulator.note: In Victoria, food businesses register with their local council under the Food Act 1984. The council classifies the business by risk and explains what you need before you can trade.

name: Mumbai
intro: Mumbai invented the modern tiffin trade: the dabbawalas have carried home-cooked lunches to offices for more than a century, and home tiffin services now feed hostels, PGs and offices across the city.
scene: Working professionals living away from home are the core market, especially in Andheri, Powai and Thane. Maharashtrian, Gujarati and Jain plans are common, and many kitchens deliver through the dabbawala network or their own riders.
price: Lunch-only plans commonly run ₹2,400 to ₹4,000 a month, and lunch-and-dinner plans ₹4,500 to ₹7,500. Single meals are usually ₹100 to ₹150.
tip: Ask for the kitchen's FSSAI registration number. It is a 14-digit number and must appear on packaging.

regulator.name: FSSAI FoSCoS portal
regulator.note: Every food business in India needs FSSAI registration or a licence through the FoSCoS portal. From 1 April 2026, basic registration covers annual turnover up to ₹1.5 crore (previously ₹12 lakh).

name: Bengaluru
intro: Bengaluru's tech corridors have made it India's busiest market for app-free, subscription tiffins aimed at people who moved to the city for work.
scene: Customers come from every state, so North Indian, Andhra, Bengali and Kerala-style plans compete side by side. Whitefield and Electronic City have so many kitchens that a trial week costs little more than a few restaurant meals.
price: Expect ₹2,400 to ₹4,000 a month for lunch only and ₹4,500 to ₹7,500 for lunch and dinner. Office delivery to tech parks can add a small fee.
tip: Tech-park gate rules change often. Confirm the kitchen can deliver to your gate or reception, not just the main road.

regulator.name: FSSAI FoSCoS portal
regulator.note: Register on FoSCoS before selling. From 1 April 2026, basic FSSAI registration covers annual turnover up to ₹1.5 crore.
